file_insights.changes_summary: Enhanced modal component with comprehensive accessibility features
key_modifications: Added focus management system with previouslyFocusedElement tracking
Implemented focus trap functionality for keyboard navigation within modal
Added Tab key handler with shift+tab support for cycling through focusable elements
Added ARIA attributes: aria-modal="true" and aria-labelledby linking
Added ID to modal title ({{ modal_id }}-title) for aria-labelledby reference
Implemented automatic focus to first focusable element on modal open
Implemented focus restoration to trigger element on modal close

patterns_discovered.description: Modal implements complete focus lifecycle: store → trap → restore pattern
patterns_discovered.implementation_details: Uses document.activeElement to track focus state, $nextTick for timing, and $watch for reactivity

patterns_discovered.description: Keyboard navigation constrained within modal using Tab/Shift+Tab cycling
patterns_discovered.implementation_details: Queries focusable elements, checks document.activeElement position, cycles focus with preventDefault

patterns_discovered.description: Accessibility features deeply integrated with Alpine.js lifecycle
patterns_discovered.implementation_details: Uses $watch for state changes, $nextTick for DOM timing, $el for element access, @ event bindings

patterns_discovered.description: Combines role="dialog" with aria-modal and aria-labelledby for full accessibility semantics
patterns_discovered.implementation_details: Provides multiple layers of meaning for assistive technologies

gotchas_discovered.issue: Modal may have CSS transitions that delay visual appearance; focus timing must account for this
gotchas_discovered.solution_implemented: Uses $nextTick() to defer focus to next tick after state change

gotchas_discovered.issue: Must capture all focusable elements including custom tabindex, excluding disabled tabindex="-1"
gotchas_discovered.potential_issue: May miss custom focusable elements not covered by selector

gotchas_discovered.issue: Previously focused element may no longer exist or may have been removed from DOM
gotchas_discovered.solution_implemented: Null check before focus() call; sets to null after restoration

gotchas_discovered.gotcha: Tab trap with single focusable element
gotchas_discovered.issue: Modal with only one focusable element will have first === last, causing focus cycling
gotchas_discovered.solution_implemented: Code will work but may feel unintuitive; no special handling needed

approach_outcome.implementation_strategy: Incremental enhancement of existing modal component with layered accessibility features
approach_outcome.maintainability: moderate - complex Alpine.js logic embedded in template

recommendations.suggestion: Extract complex Alpine.js object and event handlers into a separate JavaScript component/Alpine plugin
recommendations.rationale: Current template has 54 lines of complex logic mixed with markup; harder to test and maintain

recommendations.suggestion: Add unit/integration tests for focus management and focus trap functionality
recommendations.rationale: Focus management is critical for accessibility; behavior should be verified across browsers and edge cases

recommendations.suggestion: Document the focusable element selector and any limitations or special handling required
recommendations.rationale: Selector doesn't catch custom focusable components; developers need to understand when to extend it

recommendations.suggestion: Add check for modal with zero focusable elements; provide fallback behavior
recommendations.rationale: Current code assumes at least one focusable element exists

recommendations.suggestion: Verify focus() behavior on all target browsers, particularly with shadow DOM or custom elements
recommendations.rationale: Focus management can have subtle browser differences
